AN ACT to amend the public service law, in relation to directing the public
service commission study the feasibility and the costs of burying all or most
of the electrical, telephone and internet transmission lines in New York state
and to publish and deliver a report of its findings to the governor and the
legislature, and requiring new electrical, telephone and internet transmission
lines to be buried underground

approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 155 Chapter 805
 
      MEMORANDUM filed with Assembly Bill Number 2330-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT directing the public service commission to study the feasi-
        bility and the costs of burying all or most of  the  electrical,
        telephone  and Internet transmission lines in New York state and
        to publish and deliver a report of its findings to the  governor
        and the legislature, and requiring new electrical, telephone and
        internet transmission lines to be buried underground"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This  bill  would direct the Public Service Commission {Commission) to
analyze the feasibility and the costs of burying underground all or most
of the existing electrical, telephone, and internet  transmission  lines
in  New  York  State.  More specifically, the bill requires the study to
analyze the economic and environmental benefits from burying such exist-
ing lines as well as the economic cost  burden  of  doing  so,  if  any,
including  an  estimate  of what the cost per utility customer would be,
the number of jobs to be created to complete the project, and a timeline
for completion of the project. The bill also requires the Commission, in
analyzing costs and benefits for the purposes of this study, to consider
the varying geographical areas of the state, and  report  separately  on
the  impact  particular  areas might have on the project. The bill would
also require the study to quantify the economic costs  and  benefits  to
utility customers of burying existing electrical, telephone and internet
transmission  lines,  disaggregate the results by utility, and calculate
the cost per customer of the  entire  cost  of  the  project  statewide,
regardless of where the customer lives, for the life of the project on a
monthly  basis.  Finally,  the bill would require the Commission, within
one year of the bill's immediate effective date, to publish its findings
on its website in a location accessible to the  public,  and  deliver  a
copy of the report to the Governor and legislative leaders.
 
  I  fully  support the need to make the state's electric grid and other
utility infrastructure more resilient and less vulnerable to damage from
storms, flooding, sea level rise and other impacts, and the underground-
ing of energy infrastructure is certainly one tool that utilities should
consider in furtherance of these goals. Indeed, I recently signed legis-
lation that will, with  agreed-upon  amendments,  require  each  of  the
state's  electric  utilities  to establish a detailed Climate Resilience
Plan that will, among other things, outline storm hardening and  resili-
ence measures the utility proposes to take over short and long term, and
detail  the utility's approach to mitigating impacts from climate change
to utility infrastructure, reducing restoration costs and  outage  times
associated with extreme weather events, and enhancing reliability. It is
likely  that  "undergrounding"  of  electric transmission infrastructure
will be among the options utilities will consider under their respective
Climate Resilience Plans.
 
  While a general study of the feasibility and the costs of underground-
ing utility infrastructure could produce some  useful  information,  the
scope  of  this  bill is overly broad, the bill contains ambiguities and
presents some technical issues, and the bill sets an unreasonably  short
time  frame  for  completion  of  the study. In addition, the Commission
lacks jurisdiction over some service providers, and therefore  it  could
 
have  difficulty  obtaining  information that would be needed to examine
some of the matters identified for study.
 
  The  Legislature  has  agreed on amendments to this bill to be enacted
next session that will, among other things,  narrow  the  scope  of  the
study;  authorize the Department of Public Service, with the cooperation
of the New York State Energy  Research  and  Development  Authority,  to
undertake  the  study; and give these entities 18 months to complete and
publish the study. The amendments will also allow the Long Island  Power
Authority  service  territory to be included in the study and make other
changes to facilitate completion of the study.
 
  Based on this agreement, I am pleased to approve this bill.
 
  The bill is approved.                          (signed) KATHY HOCHUL
 
                                ______
